analyzed_vuln.description: `ndpi_free_flow_data()` blindly frees multiple pointer fields in `ndpi_flow_struct` based on protocol-state checks, but those fields can contain attacker-controlled non-heap values due to earlier packet parsing/state corruption in the same flow object. In this PoV, `flow->protos.tls_quic_stun.tls_quic.tls_supported_versions` is non-NULL with an invalid value (0x060606...), and `ndpi_free()` calls libc `free()` on it, causing a SEGV. The root issue is missing ownership/validity guarantees before freeing flow subfields (unsafe free of untrusted/stale pointer state).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Harness `fuzz_process_packet` allocates a zeroed flow, processes one attacker-controlled packet via `ndpi_detection_process_packet`, then always calls `ndpi_free_flow`. A crafted packet that drives TLS/QUIC-related parsing so that flow protocol checks pass in `ndpi_free_flow_data()` and leaves one of the corresponding dynamic-string pointers (notably `tls_supported_versions`) set to an invalid non-allocated address will deterministically crash during teardown when `ndpi_free_flow_data()` frees it.
